complete_source_units.text: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God to Idumea: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent a dispatch to the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”
Look, I have made you insignificant among the nations; you are greatly dishonored.
The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”
If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.

If thieves came in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen enough for themselves? And if grape gatherers came in to you, would they not have left a gleaning?
How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things seized!
All the men of your covenant sent you out as far as your borders; the men at peace with you opposed you and prevailed over you. They set ambushes beneath you. There is no understanding in them.
On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.
Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,
because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.
From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.
Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.
For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.
For just as you drank on My holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.
But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.

Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

And this is the beginning of the deportation: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the deportation of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah. They will inherit the cities of the Negeb.
And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

units.Jeremiah 30:1: For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.
units.Jeremiah 30:2: Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.
units.Jeremiah 30:3: For grape gatherers came to you; they will leave you no remnants. Like thieves by night they will lay their hand upon you.
units.Jeremiah 30:4: For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible
units.Jeremiah 30:5: for your orphan to remain so that he may live. And I will live, and widows have trusted in Me.
units.Jeremiah 30:6: For thus said the Lord: Those for whom there was no law to drink the cup drank it. And you, though acquitted, certainly will not be acquitted, for you will certainly drink.
units.Jeremiah 30:7: For I swore by Myself, says the Lord, that you will become an untrodden place, a reproach, and a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be deserted for ever.
units.Jeremiah 30:8: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!
units.Jeremiah 30:9: I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.
units.Jeremiah 30:10: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.
units.Jeremiah 30:11: Idumea will become an untrodden place; everyone passing by her will hiss.
units.Jeremiah 30:12: As Sodom, Gomorrah, and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, no person will settle there, and no human being will live there.
units.Jeremiah 30:13: Like a lion he will come up from Jordan’s midst into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her. Appoint the young men over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?
units.Jeremiah 30:14: Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
units.Jeremiah 30:15: For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
units.Jeremiah 30:16: Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
units.Jeremiah 32:15: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
units.Jeremiah 32:16: and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.
units.Jeremiah 32:17: And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and gave it to the nations to whom the Lord sent me to drink:
units.Jeremiah 32:18: Jerusalem, Judah’s cities, Judah’s kings, and its rulers, to make them a desolation, an untrodden place, and a hissing;
units.Jeremiah 32:19: and Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his nobles, and all his people;
units.Jeremiah 32:20: and all his mixed population, all the Philistine kings, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and Ashdod’s remnant;
units.Jeremiah 32:21: and Idumea, the Moabite land, and Ammon’s sons;
units.Jeremiah 32:22: and all Tyre’s kings, Sidon’s kings, and the kings across the sea;
units.Jeremiah 32:23: and Dedan, Teman, Ros, and everyone shorn about his face;
units.Jeremiah 32:24: and all the mixed populations lodging in the wilderness;
units.Jeremiah 32:25: and all Elam’s kings and all the Persian kings;
units.Jeremiah 32:26: and all the kings from the east, far and near, each with his brother, and all the kingdoms upon the face of the earth.
units.Jeremiah 32:27: And say to them: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Drink, get drunk, and vomit; you will fall and certainly not rise before the sword I am sending among you.
units.Jeremiah 32:28: And when they are unwilling to receive the cup from your hand to drink, say: Thus said the Lord: You will certainly drink.
units.Jeremiah 32:29: Because I am beginning to bring harm in the city upon which My name was named, and you will certainly not be cleansed, because I am summoning a sword against those dwelling upon the earth.

units.Joel 4:1: “For look, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
units.Joel 4:2: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land
units.Joel 4:3: and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.
units.Joel 4:4: What have you to do with Me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners? Are you repaying Me a recompense? Or do you bear a sharp grudge against Me? I will speedily repay your recompense upon your heads,
units.Joel 4:5: because you took My silver and gold and brought My chosen and beautiful things into your temples,
units.Joel 4:6: and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
units.Joel 4:7: Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,
units.Joel 4:8: and I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation far away, because the Lord has spoken.”
units.Joel 4:9: Proclaim these things among the nations: Consecrate war! Rouse the fighters! Draw near and come up, all soldiers!
units.Joel 4:10: Beat your plows into swords and your sickles into lances; let the powerless say, “I am strong!”
units.Joel 4:11: Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
units.Joel 4:12: Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
units.Joel 4:13: Send out sickles, because the vintage is at hand! Enter and tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evils have multiplied.
units.Joel 4:14: Sounds rang out in the Valley of Judgment, because the Lord’s day is near in the Valley of Judgment.
units.Joel 4:15: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.
units.Joel 4:16: The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.
units.Joel 4:17: You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.
units.Joel 4:18: On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.
units.Joel 4:19: Egypt will become desolate, and Idumea a desolate plain, because of injustices concerning the sons of Judah, because they poured out righteous blood in their land.
units.Joel 4:20: But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generations upon generations.
units.Joel 4:21: “I will avenge their blood, and I will certainly not acquit.” And the Lord will dwell in Zion.
units.Ezekiel 35:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 35:2: “Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it,
units.Ezekiel 35:3: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will stretch My hand against you and make you a wilderness, and you will be laid waste.
units.Ezekiel 35:4: I will make your cities desolate, and you will be a wilderness. You will know that I am the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 35:5: Because you became an everlasting enemy and ambushed Israel’s house treacherously, by enemies’ hand, with a sword at the final time of injustice,
units.Ezekiel 35:6: therefore, I live, says the Lord, the Lord: surely you sinned unto blood, and blood will pursue you.
units.Ezekiel 35:7: I will make Mount Seir a wilderness and lay it waste, and destroy human beings and livestock from it,
units.Ezekiel 35:8: and fill the hills and your ravines with your wounded. In all your plains, those wounded by the sword will fall within you.
units.Ezekiel 35:9: I will make you an everlasting wilderness, and your cities certainly will not be inhabited again. You will know that I am the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 35:10: Because you said, “The two nations and the two countries will be mine, and I will inherit them,” and the Lord is there,
units.Ezekiel 35:11: therefore, I live, says the Lord: I will deal with you according to your hostility and make Myself known to you when I judge you.
units.Ezekiel 35:12: You will know that I am the Lord. I heard the voice of your blasphemies, because you said, “Israel’s mountains are desolate; they have been given to us for food.”
units.Ezekiel 35:13: You spoke grandly against Me with your mouth. I heard.
units.Ezekiel 35:14: Thus says the Lord: In the rejoicing of the whole earth, I will make you a wilderness.
units.Ezekiel 35:15: You will be a wilderness, Mount Seir, and all Idumea will be utterly consumed. You will know that I am the Lord their God.’”

final_full_triples.source_text: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.

target_units.text: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land
and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.

final_full_triples.relationship: shared prohibition of rejoicing at another's fall
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah forbids rejoicing and boasting over Judah's destruction and affliction. Proverbs likewise forbids rejoicing when even an enemy falls, explaining that such delight displeases the Lord.
final_full_triples.source_text: Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

target_units.text: If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up,
for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.

final_full_triples.relationship: parallel condemnation of exploiting Israel's ruin
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah forbids entering the afflicted people's gates and joining attacks on their strength. Ezekiel condemns Mount Seir for claiming the two countries and treating Israel's desolate mountains as food, describing another form of exploitation of Israel's calamity.
final_full_triples.source_text: Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.

target_units.text: Because you said, “The two nations and the two countries will be mine, and I will inherit them,” and the Lord is there,
therefore, I live, says the Lord: I will deal with you according to your hostility and make Myself known to you when I judge you.
You will know that I am the Lord. I heard the voice of your blasphemies, because you said, “Israel’s mountains are desolate; they have been given to us for food.”
You spoke grandly against Me with your mouth. I heard.

final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah forbids blocking escape routes to destroy or confine fugitives. Ezekiel accuses Mount Seir of treacherously ambushing Israel's house with the sword; both condemn violence directed at Israel in its distress.
final_full_triples.source_text: Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.

target_units.text: Because you became an everlasting enemy and ambushed Israel’s house treacherously, by enemies’ hand, with a sword at the final time of injustice,

final_full_triples.relationship: parallel repayment upon the aggressor's head
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah announces that a nation's own actions will be repaid upon its head. Joel uses that same repayment language when condemning the seizure of treasures and the sale of Judah's people.
final_full_triples.source_text: For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.

target_units.text: What have you to do with Me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners? Are you repaying Me a recompense? Or do you bear a sharp grudge against Me? I will speedily repay your recompense upon your heads,
because you took My silver and gold and brought My chosen and beautiful things into your temples,
and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,

final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah moves from drinking on the holy mountain to the nations drinking and going down. In the Jeremiah account, the nations receive the Lord's wine cup of judgment, with Jerusalem and Judah heading the listed recipients. Both connect the city's judgment with that of the nations; Jeremiah explicitly names the cup.
final_full_triples.source_text: For just as you drank on My holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.

target_units.text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.
And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and gave it to the nations to whom the Lord sent me to drink:
Jerusalem, Judah’s cities, Judah’s kings, and its rulers, to make them a desolation, an untrodden place, and a hissing;

final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah locates salvation on Mount Zion. Joel likewise locates escape on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem within the promise that those calling on the Lord's name will be saved.
final_full_triples.source_text: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

target_units.text: Everyone who calls upon the Lord’s name will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be one who escapes, as the Lord said, and bearers of good news whom the Lord has called.”

final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah says Mount Zion will be holy as Jacob receives possession. Joel presents the Lord dwelling on His holy mountain and Jerusalem becoming a holy city, sharing the restoration's holiness setting.
final_full_triples.source_text: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

target_units.text: You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.

final_full_triples.relationship: Israel as the agent of judgment on Idumea
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah pictures Jacob and Joseph as fire consuming Esau's stubble. Ezekiel states that the Lord will place His vengeance on Idumea by the hand of His people Israel; both place Israel in the role of executing that judgment.
final_full_triples.source_text: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.

target_units.text: I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

final_full_triples.relationship: parallel inheritance of Edom by Jacob
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah includes possession of Esau's mountain in Israel's future holdings. Balaam's oracle likewise calls Edom and Esau an inheritance and speaks of one arising from Jacob.
final_full_triples.source_text: Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

target_units.text: And Edom shall become an inheritance, and Esau, his enemy, shall become an inheritance; Israel acted with strength.
And one shall arise from Jacob and destroy whoever escapes from a city.

final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah promises possession of Esau's mountain and further territories. Ezekiel records Mount Seir's claim to possess the two countries and Israel's desolate mountains; the passages present opposing claims and a reversal of who will possess the land.
final_full_triples.source_text: Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

target_units.text: Because you said, “The two nations and the two countries will be mine, and I will inherit them,” and the Lord is there,
therefore, I live, says the Lord: I will deal with you according to your hostility and make Myself known to you when I judge you.
You will know that I am the Lord. I heard the voice of your blasphemies, because you said, “Israel’s mountains are desolate; they have been given to us for food.”

final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah links Jerusalem's deportation with future inheritance of cities in the Negeb. Jeremiah promises renewed acquisition of fields, explicitly including the Negeb's cities, because the Lord will bring back the exiles. The connection concerns restored possession rather than identifying Obadiah's Ephrathah with another place.
final_full_triples.source_text: And this is the beginning of the deportation: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the deportation of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah. They will inherit the cities of the Negeb.

target_units.text: Fields will again be acquired in the land of which you say, It is untrodden by people and animals, and they were handed over to the Chaldeans.

They will acquire fields with silver, and you will write a document, seal it, and call witnesses in Benjamin’s land, around Jerusalem, in Judah’s cities, the hill-country cities, the cities of the Shephelah, and the cities of the Negeb, because I will bring back their exiles.

final_full_triples.relationship: parallel judgment on Esau through God's people
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah describes saved men ascending from Zion to execute judgment on Esau's mountain. Ezekiel similarly says the Lord's vengeance on Idumea will be carried out by His people Israel.
final_full_triples.source_text: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

target_units.text: I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

final_full_triples.relationship: shared kingship of the Lord over the nations
final_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah concludes that the kingdom will belong to the Lord after judgment on Esau. The psalm declares that kingship belongs to the Lord and that He rules the nations, setting the individual oracle within that wider sovereignty.
final_full_triples.source_text: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

target_units.text: All the limits of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow down before Thee,
because kingship belongs to the Lord, and He is master of the nations.

final_amended_full_triples.rationale: Both Idumea oracles connect the heart's pride or insolence with holes in rocks and an elevated position. Obadiah voices the inhabitant's boast as a question about who can bring him down. Jeremiah announces that the Lord will bring the addressee down despite the elevated eagle's nest.
final_amended_full_triples.source_text: The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”

target_units.text: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.

final_amended_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah describes soaring like an eagle and placing a nest among the stars, then announces that the Lord will bring the addressee down from there. Jeremiah likewise joins the elevated eagle's nest with the Lord bringing the addressee down.
final_amended_full_triples.source_text: If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.

target_units.text: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.

final_amended_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah describes Esau searched out and his hidden things seized. Jeremiah likewise names Esau, then says their secrets are uncovered and they cannot hide, preserving that passage's change to plural pronouns.
final_amended_full_triples.source_text: How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things seized!

target_units.text: For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible

final_amended_full_triples.relationship: parallel loss of the wise and their counsel
final_amended_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah announces destruction of the wise out of Idumea and understanding out of Mount Esau. Jeremiah's Idumea oracle addresses the loss of wisdom in Teman and counsel among the discerning.
final_amended_full_triples.source_text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.

target_units.text: For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.

final_amended_full_triples.rationale: Obadiah describes Teman's warriors terrified so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau. Jeremiah joins judgment concerning Teman with Idumea's strong men's hearts becoming like the heart of a woman in labor.
final_amended_full_triples.source_text: Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,

target_units.text: Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
